expectations.name: 01-page-written
expectations.text: A runbook is written under docs/runbooks/, the kind the map gives what to do when a trigger fires.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The runbook opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-reason-told
expectations.text:
The runbook says why it exists, told as it happened: the worker stayed down after a deploy and receipts stopped
until someone who knew the fix was found, not only a conclusion such as "receipts can stop".
expectations.evidence: The intro tells what happened: "Written after the September 14 incident: receipts stopped overnight, and on an earlier occurrence volunteers waited until noon for Tomás." The deploy cause appears later: "The September chat attributes the stopped worker to a deployment script that restarted only the web app." Step 1 adds that "`inactive (dead)` matches the September incident." Together these give the concrete events (worker down after a deploy, receipts stopped overnight, waiting until noon for the one person who knew the fix), not just a conclusion. The account is split across the document rather than told as one story.

expectations.name: 05-fact-stated
expectations.text: The runbook gives the query that counts the waiting jobs in procrastinate_jobs.
